neighbours.label: a verb of resting or standing on a supporting surface (rests on, standing on, sits on)
fire: The heavy glass top rests on four iron legs.
The ice you are standing on is only a few inches thick.
The statue sits on a tall granite pedestal in the square.
A concrete slab rests on the steel beams of the bridge.
The old house stands on wooden stilts above the marsh.
Each shelf rests on two small brackets screwed to the wall.
The lamp was sitting on a stack of old books.
The whole tower stands on a bed of solid rock.
quiet: The heavy glass top was made by a local craftsman.
The ice you are looking at is only a few weeks old.
The statue was carved by a famous artist in the square.
A concrete slab was poured last month for the bridge.
The old house was painted bright blue above the marsh.
Each shelf was sanded and varnished before it was hung.
The lamp was bought at a market with some old books.
The whole tower was designed by a young architect.

notes: Card: ' standing', ' rests', ' rested', ' sits', ' built' before 'on'; logit effect promotes over/above/atop/rest, suppresses beneath/under/below.
